verdict.rationale: Inngest ships an official self-hosting guide and a public GitHub repo explicitly supporting 'Deploy your functions to your own infrastructure... sync with a self-hosted Inngest server' (inngest-docs-9, inngest-gh-1), so the core product can be self-hosted. However, community evidence flags that the license (SSPL) is 'source available,' not true open source, calling the marketing 'deceptive' and citing OSI's 'fauxpen' characterization (inngest-comm-2, inngest-comm-11, inngest-comm-12), which tempers the openness claim even though the self-hosting mechanism itself works. Missing for 10: independent hands-on confirmation of a successful self-hosted deployment, and clarity on which features/parity gaps exist between self-hosted and cloud versions.
